replaces.change: The bundled burrito bowl poured 50 g of soy sauce (2,747 mg sodium) over a bowl whose other flavors are honey, sesame oil, and lime - it tasted only of salt and cost 1,393 mg/serving. The rewrite keeps the honey-chipotle idea on beans and rice, seasons the bowl with a quarter of that soy, and gets heat and smoke from chipotle in adobo instead. Added corn and spinach for a more balanced bowl; dropped the 50 g of sesame oil to a tablespoon of neutral oil.

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: half a red onion, very thinly sliced

ingredients.name: chipotle in adobo
ingredients.note: one pepper pulled from the can, minced, plus a spoon of sauce

steps.text: Start the rice first. Rinse 88 g of long-grain rice until the water runs clear, then cook it in a lidded pot with a pinch of salt by your preferred method; it should be done in about 18 minutes.
Make the glaze while the rice cooks: stir the soy sauce, honey, minced chipotle with a spoonful of its sauce, and half the lime juice together in a small bowl.
Char the corn: heat a dry skillet over high heat, add the kernels, and let them sit undressed in the pan for 2-3 minutes until blistered in spots, then tip them out and season with a little salt.

Build the beans in the same skillet: warm the oil over medium heat, cook the garlic for 30 seconds, add the drained beans and the glaze, and simmer for 3-4 minutes, pressing a few beans against the pan so the sauce thickens and clings.
Wilt the spinach into the bean pan for the last minute, just until collapsed, then finish with a squeeze of lime.
Quick-pickle the onion: toss the sliced red onion with the remaining lime juice and a small pinch of salt and let it sit while you assemble.
Assemble the bowls: rice on the bottom, then beans with their glaze, spinach, charred corn, diced tomato, avocado, and the pickled onion on top.

nutrition_per_serving.basis: USDA FoodData Central values committed in apps/ios/Resources/usda_ingredient_catalog.sqlite (matched fdc_id per ingredient in tables/nutrition-map.json), plus the app's shipped core-ingredient table (data.json) for items without an fdc_id; scaled by evidenced gram quantities
